answer: An AI‑agent registry anchors its admission gate to a beacon that measures the tide of recent registrations and raises proof‑of‑work difficulty accordingly. Each node must solve a hash puzzle whose target halves for every 10 % rise in the last‑hour registration rate, so a batch of 50 Sybil identities forces each to perform ≈4 × 10^12 SHA‑256 hashes, costing about 0.6 USD of compute energy per fake. The attacker therefore must spend that amount and wait the hour‑long difficulty window before any identity is accepted.
